surveycore Package Development

Source: CLAUDE.md

Part of the surveyverse ecosystem — see there for ecosystem vision, architecture, and how surveycore relates to other packages.

surveycore is the foundation package of the surveyverse ecosystem — a modern, tidyverse-compatible replacement for survey and srvyr. It provides S7-based survey design objects, a metadata/label system, and vendored variance estimation code. License: GPL-3.

The package API is stable. All core functionality is complete. New analysis functions may be added but the existing structure will not change in breaking ways. For implementation history, see git log, release tags (v0.1.0–v1.0.0), and archive/ planning directories.

Class Naming Conventions

  • S7 classes: survey_base, survey_taylor, survey_replicate, survey_twophase, survey_metadata, survey_nonprob
  • GLM fit class: survey_glm_fit (constructor function is survey_glm())
  • Result classes: survey_mean, survey_total, survey_freq, etc. (S3 built on tibble)

Naming Conventions

  • Analysis functions: get_freqs(), get_means(), get_diffs(), get_corr(), get_totals(), get_quantiles(), get_ratios()
  • Metadata getters: extract_var_label(), extract_val_labels(), extract_question_preface(), extract_var_note()
  • Metadata setters (single): set_var_label(), set_val_labels(), set_question_preface(), set_var_note()
  • Metadata setters (plural): set_variable_labels(), set_value_labels(), set_question_prefaces(), set_variable_notes()
  • Internal helpers: prefix with . (e.g., .extract_haven_labels())

Key Implementation Rules

Design variables are sacred — never remove or silently rename design variables. Always warn when weight column is modified.

Metadata lifecycle — auto-delete metadata on select() removal; auto-rename on rename(); track transformation history in @metadata@transformations.

Domain estimation vs physical subsetting — filter() keeps all rows and marks domain membership; subset() removes rows and issues a strong warning.

Internal weight column name — use "..surveycore_wt.." when converting probs to weights internally (avoids collision with user columns named .weights).

Workflow Requirements

  • Every non-trivial change lives on a feature branch — never commit implementation code to main

See .claude/rules/github-strategy.md for branching model, branch naming, and Conventional Commits format. See .claude/rules/r-package-conventions.md for devtools::document() and devtools::check() cadence.

Git Workflow

  • When asked to commit and create a PR, always target the develop branch unless explicitly told otherwise. Never assume main is the target.
  • When the user asks for a simple git push, just push. Do not invoke the full commit/PR skill workflow unless explicitly requested.

CI / Package Development

  • For R package CI (pkgdown, R CMD check): always guard vignette chunks that depend on optional/in-development packages with eval = requireNamespace("pkg", quietly = TRUE). Test locally before pushing.
  • Test warning baseline: 369. The full suite (LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 Rscript -e 'devtools::test()') raises 369 pre-existing warnings on develop, measured 2026-10-29 at 46c2b4d with surveytidy and srr not installed (#167). By source: 120 are glm()’s “contrasts dropped” warning, 104 the survey_nonprob SRS-approximation warning, 84 AAPOR small-cell warnings, and 61 others. A PR must leave that set unchanged: assert any warning it adds with expect_warning(class = ). The figure of 256 in the archive entries below is what those arcs measured at the time.

R Package Conventions

  • Use the GSS dataset (not NHANES or gss_2024) for examples and tests unless told otherwise. Use rlang patterns over deparse().
  • All R code written in any context — .R source files, roxygen2 @examples blocks, and ```r ``` blocks in .md spec and plan documents — must follow the rules in .claude/rules/code-style.md.

General Behavior

  • Before reading many files, check if the user’s question can be answered from context already available. Prefer concise answers over exhaustive file exploration.

Project Structure

  • Skills are located in .claude/skills/ (e.g., .claude/skills/spec-workflow/). Always check there first when referencing or modifying skills.

R CMD Check Gotchas

Examples must load Imports packages explicitly. R CMD check runs examples in a fresh session with only library(surveycore) loaded. If an example calls a bare function from an Imports package, add library(pkg) at the top of the block. In practice surveycore examples only call its own exported API, so this rarely bites — but keep it in mind.

Read the ARCHIVED block at the top first: the checkboxes were never marked, one task was deliberately dropped, and every measurement in the file predates #181
  • archive/haven-labelled/ — haven_labelled handling: designs strip the class on every @data write and on entry to all four constructors, survey_data(haven_class = TRUE) rebuilds it, the survey-package conversion routes capture metadata, set_val_labels() accepts a labelled column, and polychoric accepts whole-valued doubles (shipped; PRs #186–#204). Read decisions-haven-labelled.md first: it records seven SETTLED decisions, D1 to D7, and three of them resolve a HOLD. The planning documents were corrected nine times against measurement during the build. Nine documents the decisions cite are not in the repository — the pipeline archived no measurement artifacts until issue #217. Every citation of them carries [not archived], and each affected file lists them below its title
  • archive/svydesign-replicate-bridge/ — the two replicate conversion routes in R/methods-conversion.R: from_svydesign() now expands survey’s compressed replicate matrix, generates column names when survey supplies none, writes one column per replicate on every conversion, folds the base weight into a factor-form matrix, and refuses four unusable sources; as_svydesign() drops the FPC with a typed warning, refuses a design naming no replicate column, and recovered Fay’s shrinkage factor from the recorded scale until issue #243 replaced the recovery with a stored rho (shipped; issues #197, #198; PRs #239, #241, #247, #249, #250). Read decisions-svydesign-replicate-bridge.md first: it holds 19 decisions, D11 to D19 all recorded during the build rather than the planning. Four matter to anyone reading the gates. D12: gate 2’s “0 warnings” is unmeetable — clean develop carried 256 pre-existing AAPOR small-cell warnings at the time (369 as of 2026-10-29; see CI / Package Development), so the gate reads as “no new warning”. D16: gate 9 cannot run as written — air is a CLI here, not an R package, and 24 files repo-wide are already not air-clean, so the gate reads as “the PR’s own files pass air format --check”. D17: spec.md §V.2 carried a {qty()} erratum that would have made a typed-condition test impossible to pass; the spec copy here is corrected and says so under §Errata applied at archive time. D11: test-spec row ids were stripped from every builder task list, so no test block is named after a row
  • archive/as-svydesign-bridge/ — as_svydesign() and as_tbl_svy() accept a survey_nonprob design: a fourth dispatch branch routes on the shape of the weights, sending a design that names replicate weights to the replicate helper and one that names none to the Taylor helper behind the new warning surveycore_warning_nonprob_srs_conversion; as_tbl_svy() gained the input class with no body edit, because its guard already tested survey_base (shipped; issue #237; PR #259). Read decisions-as-svydesign-bridge.md first, then §Out of the spec — that section is unusually load-bearing, because D-9 narrowed this work from two issues to one and moved the replicate FPC to the neighbouring arc. Four things a later reader needs. The spec names four deferred issues, none of them a defect in this PR: #245 the dropped domain restriction, #246 the consolidation of eight in-place copies of the nonprob routing predicate, #248 a class validator weaker than the constructor that feeds it, and #251 two documentation corrections that had to wait for the warning they describe. Two planner errata survive in the plan and test-spec: both write ncol(survey::weights(converted, "analysis")), which cannot run — survey registers a method for the base weights generic and exports no function of that name — so the shipped block uses stats::weights(); and AC-6 asks for “the two pre-approved notes only” where the run has one pre-approved note plus a pre-existing .git hidden-file note that .Rbuildignore causes and this PR cannot fix. The coverage Before column is empty: both baseline attempts were killed by a low-memory watchdog at 2.06 GB free, so judge the 95% floor, which the measured 96.24% clears, and not a delta. The merge took three CI cycles and none of them failed: branch protection requires an up-to-date head branch, repository auto-merge is refused, and two other sessions merged into develop meanwhile — see prs/pr-1-as-svydesign-bridge/shipper.md, which records that updating the branch before opening the PR would have cost one cycle instead of three
  • archive/as-svydesign-domain/ — as_svydesign() on a filtered design returns the domain and not the full stored sample: one internal helper indexes the converted object with [ on the marker column, each of the three routes calls it once, the two-phase route removes no row and gives excluded rows an infinite probability (true of twophase2 only — corrected in archive/domain-marker-logical/, PR #279), and the roxygen and changelog landed last (shipped; issue #245; PRs #263, #266, #267, #268, #269, #270). Read decisions-as-svydesign-domain.md first: D1 to D17, then one record per PR. Three things a later reader needs. PR 4 drew the arc’s only tester BLOCK, for three blocks that asserted nothing about conditions. Gates 4 and 5 of PR 4’s first run died to the host’s memory watchdog and were re-run as a detached process, so the gate logs stay in the run directory and are not archived. One deferred item carries no GitHub issue, unlike #246, #261, #262 and #265: the stored call surviving the restriction is pinned on the Taylor route only
  • archive/domain-marker-logical/ — the domain marker column is logical everywhere, and an NA marker means outside the domain: a survey_base validator rejects a non-logical marker at the write, .apply_domain() resolves NA to FALSE, .restrict_to_domain() drops the coercion the validator made dead, and the printed Domain: n of N line is proved to agree with the analysis count (shipped; issue #262; PRs #272, #273, #274, #275, #277, #278, #279). Read decisions-domain-marker-logical.md first: D1 to D26, of which D21 to D26 were recorded during the build rather than the planning. Five things a later reader needs. D23 is the one that cost a BLOCK: spec.md names no analysis function anywhere, so the six functions test-spec.md §3 fixes by name were unreachable for a builder forbidden to read the test-spec — a closed list that lives in only one of the two artifacts cannot be hit. D26 corrects the plan’s own ordering rationale: PR 6 was ordered after PR 4 because PR 4 “changes the count they compare against”, and that holds for one row of four; .print_domain_info() counts straight off the marker column and never calls .apply_domain(). D25 records a defect found and deferred, not fixed in place: .restrict_to_domain() tested only the twophase2 class, so a method = "approx" design was returned unrestricted with nothing signalled; it became issue #276 and shipped as PR #279 with its own test row. The two two-phase classes are not interchangeable: [ on a twophase2 object keeps every row and voids the excluded ones to Inf, [ on a twophase object removes them, so the observable is the finite-probability count on one and the row count on the other — measured at 312/156 against 156/156. One planner erratum survives in the archived test-spec: §5 says sum(mask) gives the expected count for rows 5.2 to 5.4, which is wrong for row 5.3 — the two-phase row needs sum(mask & subset), 52 against 149 on the fixture. The shipped block asserts the corrected count; D25 records it
  • archive/replicate-oracle-tests/ — the oracle rule, and nine oracle blocks that can actually fail: tests/testthat/test-variance-replicate.R gains a no-warning and a stored-scale assertion on the eight agreeing blocks, whole rewrites of JK1 and JK2, four new blocks for JKn, bootstrap, other and Fay, and its first test_invariants() call; .claude/rules/testing-surveycore.md gains the oracle rule in three parts (shipped; issues #256, #257; PRs #281–#289). Read decisions-replicate-oracle-tests.md first — S1 to S8, P1, P2 and findings F2, N1 to N3 — and note that its archive note at the end explains why twenty citations are marked [no such file] when the documents they name are all in this directory. Nothing under R/ changed in any of the nine PRs: the R subtree hash is identical at the arc’s first and last commit. The arc fixes no wrong default; it makes the tests able to detect one, and issues #253 and #243 own the fixes. Five things a later reader needs. The arc’s central measurement is P2: doubling a design’s stored scale leaves the point estimate bit-for-bit identical on all eight numerical types while moving the standard error by exactly sqrt(2) and both bounds by 4.5 × 10⁴ times their tolerance — which is why a block asserting only the point estimate is worthless against a scale defect, and how issue #242 stayed green for 22 releases. P1 is the other one: breaking the JK1 default to 1 turns the rewritten block red on the standard error and both bounds and nowhere else, run independently by the builder and the reviewer and agreeing to the digit. Three planner errata, all the same shape — a closed count stated in one artifact that the other artifact’s prose makes unreachable: S3, the per-type table’s fifth column, which the test-spec asks for and spec.md §III.3 does not have; S6, row 2.22’s “four of four” estimator count where §3.3 fixes the Fay block at two assertions and no estimate; and N3, a title filter that returns four when three is right. A count and the prose governing it should live in the same artifact. S4 and S5 record a rule the arc cannot satisfy: the stored-scale comment must carry three elements and the shortest plain-prose form carrying all three is 82 characters, so the 80-column limit in code-style.md is unreachable — the 13 comments and two pinned titles breach it deliberately, and air format --check, which the plan names as the formatting authority, passes because it does not rewrap comments or strings. Never count constructs in that test file with grep -c: it discusses its own constructs in comments and titles, so expect_failure reads 12 textually against 6 real calls and svrepdesign reads 18 against 14; six agents miscounted before three independent parsers agreed. Zero tester BLOCKs and zero reviewer BLOCKs across all nine PRs
  • archive/replicate-scale-jkn-bootstrap/ — the JKn and bootstrap default scale move: as_survey_replicate() now stores 1 for "JKn" and 1 / (R - 1) for "bootstrap", the six expect_failure() wrappers and two ratio assertions come out of the two oracle blocks, @param scale gains eight facts with @param rscales and @param fpc cross-referencing it, as_survey_nonprob() documents why it keeps 1 / R, and 95 new expectations pin all nine stored defaults, the frame edges, the infinite scale in the variance engine and the two-phase inheritance (shipped; issue #253; PRs #293, #296, #297, #298, #299). Read decisions-replicate-scale-jkn-bootstrap.md first: ten errata E-1 to E-10, two builder HOLDs, and the CI HOLD. Six things a later reader needs. This work moved a published standard error and raises no runtime condition, by explicit decision (spec.md §A runtime transition signal was weighed and declined), so the NEWS.md entry is the only artifact that will ever explain a 2.6% rise to a user who hits it. Six of the ten errata share one mechanism — a closed count, list or fixture fixed in one artifact and addressed to a reader forbidden to open it: E-1 “exactly one block breaks”, E-2 row 4.5’s two-file list, E-4 AC-5’s “no other line”, E-6 row 1.7’s nine values (the task ordered a test-spec.md read the builder contract forbids), E-7 criterion 1’s one-row frame, and E-9 row 2.3’s four-row literals. The rule that prevents all six: a plan task addressed to the builder must transcribe every closed value it needs, because naming the source is not enough when the source is forbidden. E-7 is the one that cost a HOLD: spec.md E7 claimed a single-row frame builds and stores the default; it cannot, because .validate_data() raises surveycore_error_single_row before the switch and tests/testthat/test-constructors.R has pinned that refusal since PR #76 — the second time that spec section misdescribed which frames the constructor refuses, so treat its list of “ordinary inputs” as unverified. The write surface is nine files, not the seven spec.md names: moving the bootstrap default breaks two blocks asserting as_survey_nonprob() and as_survey_replicate() agree numerically, which is the identity quality gate 6 deliberately breaks, so test-nonprob-bootstrap-variance.R and test-analysis-corr.R were retargeted to pin the divergence instead. The NaN branch of E1 needs whole-valued data: with real-valued weights the replicate deviation lands about 1.8e-15 off zero and the product is Inf, not NaN, so a plausible fixture tests the Inf branch twice — is.nan() is self-proving here and a drifted frame turns it red. Two percentages, opposite directions, one place each: NEWS.md carries 2.6%, the rise, and as_survey_nonprob()’s help page carries 2.5%, the fall. Arc suite 12005 → 12100 with warnings held at exactly 256 and coverage at 96.15% at all six gate runs; zero _snaps/ changes; zero tester BLOCKs and zero reviewer BLOCKs across all five PRs
  • archive/replicate-fay-rho/ — Fay’s rho: as_survey_replicate() gains rho as its fifth formal, type = "Fay" requires it and stores the scale 1 / (R * (1 - rho)^2), rho with any other type warns and is discarded, every replicate design stores the key rho, from_svydesign() carries survey’s rho across, as_svydesign() passes the stored rho in place of the deleted scale inversion, print() and summary() show it, the Fay block in test-variance-replicate.R became seven real oracle comparisons, and as_survey_twophase() refuses a survey_replicate phase 1, which reverses PR #74 (shipped; issue #243; PRs #301–#309). Read decisions.md first, then its archive note at the end. Four things a later reader needs. Every Fay standard error moved, and nothing at runtime says so: a rebuilt Fay SE is the old one divided by 1 - rho, and NEWS.md is the only record. A Fay design saved before this work has no rho key, keeps the old 1/R scale in the analysis functions, and is refused by as_svydesign() with surveycore_error_fay_rho_unrecoverable. The one STOP was a missing tolerance: PR 1’s new expect_equal() used testthat’s default of about 1.49e-8 where the plan fixed 1e-8, and the audit had reported the plan’s value. Every later builder brief demanded an explicit tolerance =, and no later PR drew a BLOCK. run-gates.sh reports a dead R CMD check as a pass: with no Status: line, gate 5 prints PASS with “Status line missing”. PR 4’s check died to the memory watchdog this way and was re-run alone. Read the status line, not the gate result. One item is deferred: issue #300, which covers update_design() with a changed replicate count. The stale X-13 comment the PR 5 reviewer found in tests/testthat/test-conversion.R was fixed after the archive, in PR #310. R/variance-replicate.R is byte-identical across the arc. Suite 12100 → 12353 with warnings held at 256, and coverage 96.15% → 96.17%. Issue #243 stays open until develop merges to main
  • archive/replicate-supplied-args/ — a supplied scale or rscales that survey overrides: as_svydesign() stops passing the two arguments where survey overrides them (#311); as_survey_replicate() refuses JKn with no rscales (#312), discards a supplied scale for BRR, JK2, ACS and successive-difference (#314) and a supplied rscales for JK2, ACS and successive-difference (#315), each with surveycore_warning_replicate_arg_ignored; test-variance-replicate.R gains nine oracle blocks for a supplied scale and one export-parity block (#316); and the rho warning gains surveycore_warning_replicate_arg_ignored as a second class, with the roxygen, NEWS.md, changelog and vignette §3.4 (#317) (shipped; issue #255; PRs #311, #312, #314, #315, #316, #317). Issue #255 was closed by hand on 2026-10-14, because closing keywords do not act on merges into develop. Read decisions.md first. Five things a later reader needs. The one BLOCK was older advice made false: PRs 2 and 3 made the unreleased NEWS.md recipes for #242 (JK2) and #253 (JKn) wrong, and the spec forbade edits to older entries. Erratum E-1 (HOLD-2) corrected both, and each recipe was measured to 1e-8: type = "other" with scale = (R-1)/R reproduces the old JK2 result, and an old JKn call also needs rscales = rep(1, R). S-1 is outside the spec: the user added the vignette edit to PR 6. PR 5 added 678 lines for 10 rows, over the 600-line flag; the reviewer traced the size to the plan’s nine one-per-type oracle blocks. PRs 3 to 6 have no shipper.md: the leader opened and merged them itself. CI hung during PRs 1 and 2: the ubuntu jobs waited in setup-r on a stalled Ubuntu mirror, and #313 added a 45-minute job limit. Issue #318 holds three older documentation gaps, deferred. PR #312 covers the JKn half of issue #244, which was already closed. Suite 12353 → 12757 with warnings held at 256, and coverage 96.17% → 96.18%. Zero tester BLOCKs and one reviewer BLOCK
